transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thank you. Um, well, I'm here because I've been having an issue with how much I'm eating. It happens mostly on these late work nights. I’ll order what I tell myself is just going to be dinner, but... it turns into a whole entrée, sides, dessert, and then I'll even grab extra snacks from my kitchen on top of it. It just ends up being way, way more food than I’d ever eat if someone were actually sitting across from me.
After eating like this, do you ever do anything to try to make up for the food, such as making yourself throw up?

No, I don't do anything like that. I've never made myself throw up or... tried to get rid of it. I usually just end up sitting there feeling uncomfortably full and pretty bad about myself, but no, I don't do anything to try and make up for the food.
During these times when you are eating so much, do you feel like you can't stop or can't control what or how much you are eating?

Yeah, that's exactly it. Once I start, there’s this point where... I'm almost just watching myself do it. I'll keep going back to the food or opening another package, and in my head, I'm thinking that I really need to stop. But it just feels like the decision has already slipped out of my hands. I just can't seem to stop once I get going.
On average, about how many times a week do these episodes of overeating happen?

Well, if I look back at my delivery receipts and my work calendar... there’s usually at least one night every week where this happens. Sometimes it's more than that, but it's consistently at least once a week. And that pattern has been going on for several months now.
